rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the emitted substance as semen deposited in the womb.
rows.anchor: İmnâ ettiğiniz, yani rahimlere döktüğünüz nutfeyi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans do not determine, shape, or create the semen into human form; God creates it from nothing.
rows.anchor: Siz mi takdir ve tasvir edip insan biçimine koyuyorsunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigns each person a fixed time of death according to the wise purposes of His will.
rows.anchor: her birinize bir vakit tâyin ederek aranızda ölümü kat‘iyyen takdir ve taksim eyledik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can surpass God, restrain His will, or prevent Him from doing as He wishes.
rows.anchor: kimse Bize üstün gelemez, irademizi alıkoyamaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differ over whether عَلَىٰ attaches to the preceding power, an ellipsis, or قَدَّرْنَا.
rows.anchor: mazmûnundaki kudrete veya mahzûfa veya قَدَّرْنَا’ya müte‘allik olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أَمْثَٰلَكُمْ can be read as the plural of misl with kasra or mathal with two fathas.
rows.anchor: mîm’in kesriyle “misl”in cem‘i olabileceği gibi, iki fetha ile “mesel”in cem‘i de olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If read as the plural of misl and linked to قَدَّرْنَا, death ends no lineage: people are replaced by their counterparts.
rows.anchor: Aranızda ölümü takdir ettik ki, neslinizi kesmek üzere değil, sizi emsâl ve eşbâhınıza tebdil etmek üzere.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If linked to the power implicit in “we are not overcome,” God can remove people and bring replacements, as in Fāṭir 35:16.
rows.anchor: sizi giderip yerinize emsâlinizi getirmek suretiyle tebdîle de kādiriz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers reading أَمْثَٰلَكُمْ with two fathas as the plural of mathal.
rows.anchor: Lâkin burada fethateyn ile “mesel”in cem‘i olması daha ziyade şâyân-ı tercihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathal conveys qualities and forms, including a person's moral character and outward appearance.
rows.anchor: “Mesel” sıfat ve şekil mânalarıyla maddî ve mânevî temsîli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing people's present forms and creating them in an unknown state encompasses worldly transformation and resurrection, carrying both threat and promise.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna hem dünyevî inkılâbâtı hem uhrevî neş’et olan ba‘si ifade eder.

rows.speaker: Hasan-ı Basrî
rows.claim: Hasan al-Baṣrī reads the passage as a threat that people may be transformed into apes and swine, like the warning in al-Nisāʾ 4:47.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî Hazretleri va‘îd cihetini mülâhaza ederek “sizi maymunlara, hınzırlara çeviririz”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the surrounding discourse concerns resurrection and recompense, he takes the changing clause as worldly upheaval and the creating clause as the subsequent resurrection.
rows.anchor: Kelâmın evvel ve âhiri ba‘s ve cezâ ve neş’et-i uhrâ ile alâkadar olduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation proceeds through recognizable stages: earth, semen, alaqa, and mudgha, observed in experience and described in the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: insanın bu dünyâ hayatta toprak, sonra nutfe, aleka,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should infer that the Creator who brought them through known transformations can resurrect them in a state they cannot now detail.
rows.anchor: bildiğiniz bu tarz-ı tehavvül ve tekâmül

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since sustenance is essential to human life and cultivation is its material or spiritual basis, the discourse turns from creation to cultivation.
rows.anchor: Hayât-ı beşerin levâzımından birisi rızk, rızıkta da esas maddî veya mânevî hars olduğu için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People can sow, but God alone makes crops take root, grow, and reach their useful end.
rows.anchor: siz mi tutturup büyütüp gayesine eren mezrû‘ât hâline getiriyorsunuz?

rows.speaker: Kurtubî
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī recommends that a farmer recite this verse after seeking refuge and the basmala, then supplicate for the crop.
rows.anchor: Kurtubî der ki: “Ekini eken ekinci eûzü besmele’den sonra bu âyeti okuyup şöyle demek müstehab olur:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accompanying supplication asks for blessing on Muhammad, provision of the crop, protection from its harm, and gratitude; it is said to have proved effective against crop calamities.
rows.anchor: Denilmiş ki bu dua ekinin âfâtını def‘ile intâcında mücerrebdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuṭām means dry fragments such as rubbish, stalks, straw, or broken husks.
rows.anchor: “Hutâm” kuru şeylerin kırıntısına denir; çörçöp, ot çöpü, saman çöpü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafakkuh literally means eating varied fruits and figuratively can mean being amazed or regretful.
rows.anchor: “Tefekküh” esasen türlü yemiş yemek demek olup mecaz olarak taaccüb etmek ve pişman olmak mânalarına da gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here tafakkuh depicts people repeatedly chewing over bewildered, regretful words as if eating them.
rows.anchor: Burada murad şaşkınlıkla şu lakırdıları yemiş yer gibi tekrar tekrar söyler, çiğner, geveler dururdunuz demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limughramun may mean heavy loss, wasted crops and expenses, or being in debt.
rows.anchor: Biz her hâlde çok ziyandayız ektiğimiz tohumlar zâyi‘oldu, yaptığımız masraflar boşa gitti, yahut borçlandık.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if gharām means destruction, the speakers mean that they are ruined and annihilated.
rows.anchor: garâm” helâk mânasına olduğuna göre; inanın helâk olduk, mahv

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maḥrūm means deprived of the food their failed crop would have supplied.
rows.anchor: biz mahrûmuz yani ektiğimiz mahv ve ziyan olduğu gibi yiyecek rızıktan da mahrûmuz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they fear that no profit remains and that they are condemned to poverty.
rows.anchor: bundan böyle hiç kazanç ihtimâli kalmamış, her şeyden mahrum, sefâlete mahkûmuz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lines may be repeated in dialogue by different people, voicing despair as though no blessing remains.
rows.anchor: Bu sözler bir cümlesini birisi, bir cümlesini diğer birisi söylemek suretiyle muhavere tarzında tekrar tekrar söylenir durur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In despair over the crop, people overlook that they still have water and that worse calamities could befall them; the discourse therefore turns to drinking water.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın bundan daha büyük felâketleri olabileceği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muzn means a cloud, or specifically a white cloud from which rain is rare.
rows.anchor: asıl “Müzn” bulut yahut ak bulut demektir ki ondan yağmur yağmak nâdir olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation says that water from the cloud is sweeter.
rows.anchor: Bir de denilmiş ki suyu daha tatlıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ujāj is salty, bitter water that cannot be drunk.
rows.anchor: Dilersek onu bir ücâc, yani tuzlu bir acı su yapardık ki içilmek ihtimâli olmazdı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crop spoilage is familiar while bitter rain is only possible; he also says food matters more than drink, explaining the lām in the crop clause and its absence in the water clause.
rows.anchor: Ekilen tohumların bazen çürüdüğü vâki‘de mâlum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two conditional clauses beginning with “if We wished” are parenthetical statements that protecting crops and water from harm is an additional blessing.
rows.anchor: Gerek evvelkinde, gerek bunda لَوْ نَشَآءُ ile başlayan iki cümle-i şartiye Allah teâlâ’nın harsı ve suyu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should thank God for each blessing instead of despairing as deprived or boasting that they cultivate when one blessing is lost.
rows.anchor: Bütün bu nimetlerden her birine şükretseniz de biri eksik oluverince hemen “mahrûmuz” diye ye’s ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire people kindle is produced by rubbing materials together, an instance of fire generated by friction and contact.
rows.anchor: birbirine sürtüp çakmak suretiyle çıkardığınız ateşi ki delk ü temas ile çıkan bir elektrik ateşi demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the fire from the tree to Yā Sīn 36:71.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Yâsîn’de geçen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree is commonly marh and afar, though the same point applies to other trees, electrical sources, and flint.
rows.anchor: ki mâruf merh u afâr’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traditional poetic line says every tree contains fire, while marh and afar are especially celebrated for it.
rows.anchor: فِي كُ ِّل شَجَرٍ نَارٌ وَاسْتَمْجَدَ الْمَرْخُ وَالْعَفَارُ denilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the electrical property in matter; without it neither a Bedouin's flint nor a modern electric lamp could produce light.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ cisimlerde o elektrik hâssasını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire is a reminder because livelihood depends on it and it exemplifies life's struggle; it also recalls the punishment of Hellfire.
rows.anchor: maîşet sebepleri kendisine rabt olunup hayat mücadelesine numûne

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means an enjoyment, useful benefit, and a means of livelihood or gain.
rows.anchor: hem de bir metâ‘, bir temettu‘, bir intifâ‘ve kazanç vâsıtası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muqwīn are desert travelers who camp and move on; they benefit especially from fire because they need to kindle it more than settled people do.
rows.anchor: ondan en ziyade onlar istifade ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes al-muqwīn as poor people with great need, who gather and sell wood when they have no other livelihood.
rows.anchor: İhtiyâcı çok olan fakirler için.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response is to glorify the great Lord as exalted above partners and imperfection, by saying Subḥāna rabbiyal-ʿaẓīm or praying.
rows.anchor: nâm-ı azametini tenzih ederek tesbih eyle yahut namaz kıl.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah encompasses every perfection, is necessary in existence, and alone has the right to divinity.
rows.anchor: sıfatlarını câmi‘Vâcibü’l-vücûd ve ulûhiyet kendinin hakkı olan bir Zât-ı ecell ü a‘lâ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no deity besides Him; the name Allah is the divine proper name encompassing all divine names, as explained in the Fātiḥa discussion of the basmala.
rows.anchor: Bütün esmâ-i ilâhiyenin câmi‘i, ism-i zât olan “Allah” ism-i celâli hakkında Fâtiha’nın başında “besmele”nin tefsirinde geçen îzâhâta bak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayb may mean absolute unseen, inaccessible to every creature, or relative unseen, unknown only to a particular creature.
rows.anchor: ne ihsâsı ne ilmi ta‘alluk etmeyendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers absolute unseen here: there is no contextual cue for a relative referent, the definite article is comprehensive, and praise favors this reading; other Qurʾānic descriptions support it.
rows.anchor: Burada mütebâdir olan ise gayb-ı mutlaktır. Çünkü ahde karîne yoktur. ال istiğrak içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, God's knowledge encompasses every unseen, whether necessary, contingent, nonexistent, or impossible.
rows.anchor: gerek vâcib ve gerek mümkin mevcud veya ma‘dum ve gerekse mümteni‘her gayba şâmil olur.

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Rāghib defines shuhūd and shahāda as presence together with perception by sight or insight, while mere presence can also be considered.
rows.anchor: Râgıb der ki: “‘Şuhûd’ ve ‘şehâdet’, gerek basar ve gerek basiret ile olsun müşahede ile beraber huzurdur.

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Rāghib says shuhūd better suits mere presence, while shahāda better suits presence accompanied by perception.
rows.anchor: ma‘a’l-müşâhede huzûra da ‘şehâdet’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnessed realm is what creatures can perceive with sight or insight; knowledge of the unseen entails knowledge of the witnessed even more certainly.
rows.anchor: âyetteki “şehâdet”ten murad mahlûkun basar veya basiret ile müşahede edebileceği âlem demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both unseen and witnessed are named to make God's exhaustive knowledge explicit, as in al-Kahf 18:49.
rows.anchor: ihsâ tamamıyla tasrih olunmak için ikisi de zikredilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm denote two kinds of divine mercy, previously explained in the Fātiḥa discussion of the basmala.
rows.anchor: Bu iki sıfat iki nevi rahmete delâlet eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raḥmānic mercy is initially bestowed without prior earning and extends to believers and unbelievers, workers and nonworkers.
rows.anchor: Rahmet-i rahmâniye hiçbir nevi kesb ile meşrut ve mesbuk olmayarak ibtidâen bahşolunan rahmet-i ilâhiyedir ki mü’mine de kâfire de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Existence, fetal and animal nourishment, and worldly provisions such as sustenance and reason even for unbelievers are examples of this initial mercy.
rows.anchor: Yine bu rahmet ile Allah teâlâ kâfirlere dahi dünyada rızık, akıl vesâire gibi nimetler verir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy associated with al-Raḥīm follows earned good use of initial mercy; its least reward is deserved, while its highest level is boundless grace.
rows.anchor: Rahmet-i rahîmiye ise kesb ile meşrut olan ve rahmet-i rahmâniyeyi hüsn-i isti‘mâl ederek çalışanlara verilen rahmettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites the formulation that God is the Merciful of this world and the Compassionate of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: رَحْمَانُ ال ُّدنـْيَا وَرَحِيمُ الآْخِرَةِ denilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥīm distinguishes faithless from faithful and good from bad, promising the good their final reward; those who misuse initial mercy incur deprivation, punishment, and responsibility, clarified in the next verse.
rows.anchor: Rahîm” sıfatı iman ile imansızı, iyi ile kötüyü, korunanlarla korunmayanları ayırt ederek iyileri âkıbet ecr ü mükâfat ile murâda erdirmek mânasını ifade ettiği için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although these verses establish awe of God's majesty and power, they begin with mercy to awaken love and hope before fear.
rows.anchor: bu âyetler mehâfetten evvel mahabbet ve ümid hislerini uyandıracak olan bu rahmet âyetiyle başlamıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge precedes mercy because complete, hidden-and-apparent reward requires perfect knowledge.
rows.anchor: rahmet-i rahîmiyenin gizli ve âşikâr hiçbir ecri zâyi‘etmeyecek vechile tamamıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oneness precedes knowledge because flawless knowledge and mercy require unity without partner or rival in essence, attributes, and acts.
rows.anchor: sıfât-ı zâtiyye-i selbiyeden olan “vahdâniyet” sıfatı da ona takdim olunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Allah is placed first because the divine essence is the source of the negative, affirmative, and active attributes.
rows.anchor: sıfât-ı selbiye ve sübûtiye ve fi‘liyenin mercii olan vücûd-ı Zat da “Allah” ism-i celâli ile hepsinden mukaddem zikrolunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haşyah is not bare fright but reverent fear accompanied by love and veneration.
rows.anchor: “haşyet” mutlak ürküntüden ibaret olan bir korku değil, mahabbet ve tâzim ile müterâfık olan saygılı bir korku demek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse first evokes reverence and hopeful love, in keeping with the sacred report that mercy precedes wrath, then prepares for the responsibility and fear contained in al-Raḥīm.
rows.anchor: gazab-ı ilâhîye sâbık olduğunu iş‘âr eden bu âyet ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening declaration is repeated to emphasize God's essence and oneness before all else; He alone is truly worthy of worship.
rows.anchor: Her şeyden evvel Zât-ı Hakk’a ve emr-i tevhîde kemâliyle ihtimam ve itinayı ibraz için tekrar ile tekid olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik means the sole owner and ruler of all visible and hidden realms, exercising command, governance, appointment, honor, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: Mülkün sâhibi bütün eşyânın mülk ü melekûtu O’nun, bütün mevcûdât üzerinde emr ü nehy, tedbîr ü tasarruf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Quddūs means supremely holy, free of every blemish, perfect in every attribute, beyond limitation or description, and immaculate.
rows.anchor: gayet mukaddes, her şâibeden münezzeh, her vasfında ekmel, tahdîd ü tasvîre sığmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Salām is the source of all safety, free from defect, deficiency, decay, and harm, and the one who grants safety to those who seek it.
rows.anchor: Selâm her selâmetin menba‘ve masdarı: Kendisi ayıbdan, kusurdan, eksiklikten, fenâ ve zevalden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾmin gives faith, security, and protection, removing doubts and granting assurance to refugees and the fearful.
rows.anchor: iman veya emniyet ve eman verici, şekleri, tereddüdleri kaldıran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muhaymin watches over all things as witness, keeper, and guardian; he refers readers to al-Māʾida 5:48.
rows.anchor: görüp gözeten, her şeye şâhid ve hafîz, nigehbân da O.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz can mean majestic and honorable, never defeated and victorious in every matter.
rows.anchor: onurlu, şanlıdır. Hiçbir vechile mağlub edilmez, her işinde gālibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss of al-ʿAzīz is that God has no equal and is supremely exalted.
rows.anchor: Yahut misli yok, gayet yüksektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further gloss is that God does whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: Yahut dilediğini yapar, “fa‘‘âlün limâ-yürîd”dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite His might, God does not love base conduct, immorality, disbelief, injustice, corruption, disobedience, or ingratitude.
rows.anchor: Bununla beraber alçaklığı, ahlâksızlığı, küfür, zulüm, fesad, isyan, küfran gibi fenalıkları sevmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jabbār is an intensive active participle from jabr, which carries two principal meanings.
rows.anchor: “Cebbâr” yukarılarda da geçtiği üzere “cebr”den mübalağalı ism-i fâildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reparative sense, jabr means restoring a broken thing and completing or correcting what is deficient.
rows.anchor: “cebr” esasen kırığı yerine getirip sıkı sarmak, eksiği ıslah edip tamamlamak demektir.

rows.speaker: Müfessirînin birçoğu
rows.claim: Many exegetes take al-Jabbār in this reparative sense: God remedies suffering, repairs brokenness, enriches the poor, and sets disorder right.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin birçoğu Allah teâlâ’ya “Cebbâr” ıtlâkı bu mânadan olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its second sense, jabr means compelling; al-Jabbār is the irresistible one who can compel creatures to His will, like al-Qahhār.
rows.anchor: “cebr” icbar etmek, yani dilediğini zorla yaptırmak mânasına da gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This name must not be read in the Jabriyya sense that humans have no will or voluntary acts.
rows.anchor: bundan cebriyyenin dediği gibi kullara hiç irade vermez, her emrini cebr ile yürütür, insanlarda ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriye yoktur mânasını da çıkarmamalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes His legislative commands conditional on people's partial will, as shown by many texts including Muḥammad 47:7.
rows.anchor: teşrî‘î olan emirlerini kulların irâde-i cüz’iyesiyle meşrut kılmış olduğu da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants freedom in many acts but is not bound to enact every human will and may remove it when He chooses.
rows.anchor: insanlara birçok fiillerde irade vermiş, hür yaratmış olmakla beraber bütün iradelerini infâza mecbur değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports a hadith saying that when God wills His decree, He may remove intelligent people's minds until it takes effect, then restore their reason and leave them regretful.
rows.anchor: bir hadîs-i şerîfte إِذَا أَرَادَ االلهُ إِنـْفَاذَ قَضَائِهِ وَقَدَرِهِ سَلَبَ ذَوِي الْعُقُولِ عُقُولَهُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may also enforce His will against people's wishes without removing their reason or will.
rows.anchor: beraber isteklerinin hilâfına olarak kendi hüküm ve iradesini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rebels may resist punishment, but when its time comes they must undergo it.
rows.anchor: ikāba yanaşmak istemedikleri hâlde vakti gelince cezâlarını çekmeye mecbur olurlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under God's absolute, decisive will nothing escapes being overpowered; he closes with Āl ʿImrān 3:83, where all submit willingly or unwillingly and return to Him.
rows.anchor: وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ طَوْعًۭا وَكَرْهًۭا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ
